text:
devon: heads up — support ticket from AcmeCorp: huge p99 jump (~600ms -> 2.3s) on their /generate route starting ~10:40 PST. Customer sees tail latency only on steady traffic (not cold starts). :eyes:

maria: any correlating deploys?

devon: we rolled tiny prefix-key normalization last night (hashing change) but rollout was gradual and flagged as safe. No infra deploys.

aj: can you paste the p95/p99 trends and kv miss rate?

maria: quick dumps:
```
# from prometheus
redwood_request_latency_seconds{route="/generate",quantile="0.99"} > 2.0
kv_prefix_cache_miss_rate{shard="s1"} spikes 0.04 -> 0.35
kv_evictions_total{policy="lru_prefix"} +2800 in 30m
```

chandra: that miss rate jump + eviction surge smells like key entropy leakage after prefix normalization change. If keys normalized differently, many prefixes won't match warm KV entries and warmup can't help -> thrash.

nate: agreed. Two quick mitigations to buy time: 1) rollback prefix normalization rollout to 0% for affected cluster, 2) temporarily increase cache capacity on s1 and lower eviction aggressiveness (raise max_entries, extend TTL).

devon: support asked for repro steps they can run. We should also give them a config to reduce p99 quickly.

aj: repro steps I used locally that reproduced tail:
1) seed 200 unique user prefixes with low TTL to simulate high cardinality
2) run steady RPS 150 qps with prompt lengths ~120 tokens
3) observe KV misses incr after ~8 minutes, p99 rises

sre-oncall-bot: deploy-alert: prefix-normalize-v2 rollout -> 18% -> coinflip routing active on s1 (10:42 PST)

maria: aha timeline matches. rollout traffic started 10:42 and p99 rose 10:50. So rollout amplified hot-key divergence.

chandra: probable root cause: we normalized client prefixes to remove trailing whitespace and lowercase, but hashing function changed from murmur3 -> xxhash64. While functionally OK, distribution changed and collisions/striping changed which affected how keys map to shards and warmup locality. Warmup (KV prefetch) assumed murmur3 buckets. We didn't invalidate warmup metadata when switching hash. Result: warm entries became unreachable -> miss -> evict -> cold loads -> thrash.

nate: good call. Tests to confirm: compute bucket mapping distribution for a representative prefix sample under both hashers and see difference entropy.

aj: I ran a quick script:
```
# python pseudocode
old = [murmur3(p) % 1024 for p in sample]
new = [xxhash64(p) % 1024 for p in sample]
common = len(set(old) & set(new)) / 1024
```
Observed ~58% overlap only. That's low for warm locality.

devon: action list: rollback normalization rollout (nate), bump cache size + relax eviction for s1 (maria), run mapping analysis (chandra + aj), customer mitigation note (nate).

maria: I'll patch autoscaler to add +25% cache capacity for cluster s1 now. Also toggling eviction policy to target age-based less aggressively.

nate: I'll trigger rollback to 0% and add a temporary feature flag to force old hasher for warmup metadata until we can migrate.

chandra: long-term fix options: 1) migrate warmup metadata via rehash mapping job (reassign warm keys from old->new) 2) keep stable hasher and only change normalization semantics that don't alter bucket mapping 3) include hasher-version as part of cache key so warmup entries coexist for a short period. I'd prefer option 3 as least disruptive.

aj: tests to add: hash-consistency unit tests, warmup migration e2e, and a rollout gating check: if warmup overlap <70% block rollout.

devon: customer update drafted: "we identified a cache key hashing change as the likely cause; we've rolled back the change for your region and increased cache capacity; we'll monitor and follow up with residual mitigation steps."

maria: monitoring hooks added: alert if kv_evictions_total spikes > 1000/min per shard and new metric kv_warmup_overlap < 0.7.

sre-oncall-bot: incident-note: mitigations applied 10:58 PST -> rollback + cache bump. p99 dropped back to ~650ms within 7m.

nate: follow-ups: run rehash-migration job window (low traffic), add migration CLI: `rehash-warmup --from=old_hasher --to=new_hasher --dry-run`, and schedule postmortem with owner chandra.

chandra: I'll own the postmortem and the migration design doc. Will also add a canary step in rollout checklist: compute warmup overlap metric and require >0.7.

devon: thanks everyone. I'll close the support ticket with customer update and attach the mitigations. :thumbsup:

maria: adding TL;DR for support: root cause = hasher+normalization changed bucket mapping -> warmup mismatch -> cache thrash -> p99 regression. Hotfixes = rollback hasher change, bump cache, relax evictions, monitor overlap metric.

aj: saving logs and scripts to runbook: `docs/runbooks/kv-warmup-migration.md` (will create).

nate: also consider adding a metric that tracks "fraction of requests served from warm cache" to detect this class of regressions earlier.

devon: agreed. We'll keep this thread as the timeline for the incident.
